verbalization: Hydroxymatairesinol is implicated in the regulation of Serine/threonine-protein kinase ATR through a multi-step mechanism involving potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 3. This target is engaged by multiple metabolites, including (2R,3R)-2-decyl-3-[(2Z,5Z)-octa-2,5-dienyl]oxirane, (1-Methylbutyl)oxirane, and a complex ester compound, all of which are metabolites of hydroxymatairesinol. The presence of multiple targets suggests a potential role in modulating cellular signaling pathways, possibly through the regulation of ion channels that influence intracellular signaling and homeostasis. The consistent involvement of potassium voltage-gated channels in this relationship implies a mechanism by which hydroxymatairesinol may influence kinase activity, potentially through the modulation of cellular ion fluxes. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between hydroxymatairesinol and ATR, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
